title: Optimal integration strategies for the multinational firm
summary_en: Multinational firms have a menu of integration strategies: source inputs at arm's length, in-house from foreign subsidiaries, or a mix. Grossman, Helpman and Szeidl model this choice and characterise when each strategy dominates as a function of contracting frictions, the input's specificity, and the relative cost of foreign vs. domestic production. Their framework provides a unified account of FDI, offshoring, and supply-chain configuration that has become a standard reference for the trade-and-multinationals literature.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No primary dataset; model is mapped to stylised facts about MNE structure (foreign affiliate output shares, intra-firm trade volumes) drawn from the trade-statistics literature.
policy_relevance: Useful framing for Hungarian FDI and industrial policy (HIPA, ITM): the paper provides the analytical lens for thinking about why MNEs choose to integrate Hungarian operations vertically (subsidiary-based assembly) vs. arm's-length sourcing, and what changes in contracting environment or trade costs would shift those choices. Particularly relevant for current Hungarian debates about supply-chain reshoring and EU industrial-policy responses.
